questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number.

65 : 5 :: 117 : ?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is :

First number ÷ 13 = Second number 

 
• 65 : 5 → 65 ÷ 13 = 5

Similarly,

 
• **117 : ? → 117 ÷ 13 = 9 **

Hence, the correct answer is **"9".**

questions.question:
By interchanging the given two signs which of the following equation will be not correct?

+ and ÷

I. 9 ÷ 6 × 4 + 2 - 5 = 16

II. 5 - 28 + 7 × 16 ÷ 4= -103
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is :-

By using BODMAS RULE :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4671232025562bc3ba9a781319d633acf8cd8e78dc8e96912cd7564a7df4717d.png] 

I. Given equation : 9 ÷ 6 × 4 + 2 - 5 = 16

After interchanging the given two symbols + and ÷ the equation is as follows : 9 + 6 × 4 ÷ 2 - 5 = 16

⇒ 9 + 6 × __**4 ÷ 2**__ - 5 = 16

⇒ 9 + __**6 × 2**__ - 5 = 16

⇒ __**9 + 12**__ - 5 = 16

⇒ __**21 - 5**__ = 16

⇒ 16 = 16

LHS = RHS

II. Given equation : 5 - 28 + 7 × 16 ÷ 4= -103

After interchanging the given two symbols + and ÷ the equation is as follows : 5 - 28 ÷ 7 × 16 + 4 = -103

⇒ 5 - __**28 ÷ 7**__ × 16 + 4 = -103

⇒ 5 - __**4 × 16**__ + 4 = -103

⇒ __**5**__ - 64 __**+ 4**__ = -103

⇒ __**9**____** - 64**__ = -103

⇒ **-55 ≠ -103**

**LHS ≠ RHS**

∴ Here, Conclusion II is not correct.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Only II".**

questions.question:
Which two numbers should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

1 × 4 + 3 - 5 = 6
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is :-

By using BODMAS RULE :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4671232025562bc3ba9a781319d633acf8cd8e78dc8e96912cd7564a7df4717d.png] 

Option 1) : 1 and 5

Given equation is : 1 × 4 + 3 - 5 = 6

After interchanging the two number the equation is as follows : 5 × 4 + 3 - 1 = 6

⇒ __**5 × 4**__ + 3 - 1 = 6

⇒ __**20 + 3**__ - 1 = 6

⇒ __**23 - 1**__ = 6

⇒ 22 ≠ 6

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 2) : 4 and 5

Given equation is : 1 × 4 + 3 - 5 = 6

After interchanging the two number the equation is as follows : 1 × 5 + 3 - 4 = 6

⇒ __**1 × 5**__ + 3 - 4 = 6

⇒ __**5 + 3**__ - 4 = 6

⇒ __**8 - 4**__ = 6

⇒ 4 ≠ 6

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 3) : 5 and 3

Given equation is : 1 × 4 + 3 - 5 = 6

After interchanging the two number the equation is as follows : 1 × 4 + 5 - 3 = 6

⇒ __**1 × 4**__ + 5 - 3 = 6

⇒ __**4 + 5**__ - 3 = 6

⇒ __**9 - 3**__ = 6

⇒ **6 = 6**

**LHS = RHS**

Option 4) : 3 and 6

Given equation is : 1 × 4 + 3 - 5 = 6

After interchanging the two number the equation is as follows : 1 × 4 + 6 - 5 = 3

⇒ __**1 × 4**__ + 6 - 5 = 3

⇒ __**4 + 6**__ - 5 = 3

⇒ __**10 - 5**__ = 3

⇒ 5 ≠ 3

LHS ≠ RHS

Hence, the correct answer is **"5 and 3".**

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word.

Hooghly : Kolkata :: Ganga : ?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: The second word is a city on the bank of the river mentioned in the first word.

Here,

Hooghly : Kolkata → Kolkata is a city on the bank of the Hooghly River.

Similarly,

Ganga : ? → Patna is a city on the bank of the Ganga River.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Patna"**.

questions.question:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions based on those statements. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

**Statements:**

I. No X is S.

II. All J are X.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some S are not X.

II. Some J are not S.

III. Some J are not X.

options.text: Both conclusions I and III follows
Both conclusions I and II follows

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/02d7bfdc5f07a2cf245c9ace64d192d79217203efd2bed3bec8b945c7f22d897.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some S are not X → True (As No X is S so, Some S are not X is true)

II. Some J are not S → True (As No X is S and All J are X so, Some J are not S is true)

III. Some J are not X → False (As All J are X so, Some J are not X is false)

∴ Here, Both conclusions I and II are true.

Hence, the correct answer is** "Both conclusions I and II follows".**

questions.question: Seven students, Annie, Billy, Carrie, Disha, Esha, Faisal, and Gayatri scored different marks. Disha scored more than Faisal who scored second best. Three students have scored between Carrie and Faisal. Gayatri has scored less than Carrie. Who has scored the least?
questions.solution:
Seven students, Annie, Billy, Carrie, Disha, Esha, Faisal, and Gayatri scored different marks.

1) Disha scored more than Faisal who scored second best.

Disha > Faisal

2) Three students have scored between Carrie and Faisal. 

Disha > Faisal > ___ > ___ > ___ > Carrie.

3) Gayatri has scored less than Carrie.

Disha > Faisal > ___ > ___ > ___ > Carrie > Gayatri.

∴ Here, 'Gayatri' scored the least marks.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Gayatri".**
